glosses: полигр. заголовочный текст или иные данные, помещаемые над или под основным текстом страницы или нескольких страниц книги, газеты, журнала, электронного документа и т. п.

examples.text: Обычно верхний колонтитул располагается в верхнем поле, а нижний — в нижнем поле, хотя MS Word позволяет разместить колонтитулы в любом месте страницы.

glosses: The upper portion of a page (or other) layout.

examples.text: If you reduce the header of this document, the body will fit onto a single page.

glosses: Text, or other visual information, used to mark off a quantity of text, often titling or summarizing it.

examples.text: Your header is too long; "Local Cannibals" will suffice.

glosses: Text, or other visual information, that goes at the top of a column of information in a table.

examples.text: That column should have the header "payment status".

glosses: A font, text style, or typesetting used for any of the above.

examples.text: Parts of speech belong in a level-three header. Level-two headers are reserved for the name of the language.

glosses: The first part of a file or record that describes its contents.

examples.text: The header includes an index, an identifier, and a pointer to the next entry.

glosses: Clipping of header file.
the first part of a packet or stream, often containing its address and descriptors.

examples.text: The encapsulation layer adds an eight-byte header and a two-byte trailer to each packet.

glosses: A brick that is laid sideways (on its largest face), for example at the top of a wall or within the brickwork, with its smallest side showing (oriented so that that side is wider than it is tall).

examples.text: This wall has four header courses.

glosses: A horizontal structural or finish piece over an opening.
A machine that separates and gathers the heads of grain etc.

examples.text: They fed the bale into the header.

glosses: The act of hitting the ball with the head.

examples.text: His header for the goal followed a perfect corner kick.
The Black Cats had a mountain to climb after James Morrison's header and Shane Long's neat side-foot finish gave Albion a 2-0 lead five minutes in.

glosses: Someone who heads the ball.
A headlong fall, jump or dive.

examples.text: The clown tripped over the other clown and took a header.
"When the rest are in, you see one or two shiverin' on the bank, envyin' the others that have taken the plunge. It's the last that have the worst of it. I'm all for a header and have done with it."

glosses: A raised tank that supplies water at constant pressure, especially to a central heating and hot water system.
A pipe which connects several smaller pipes.

examples.text: Common practice is to use plastic pipes with iron headers.

glosses: The rodeo performer who drives the steer toward the heeler to be tied.
One who puts a head on something.
A headcase; a nutjob (mentally unbalanced, unpredictable person).
To strike (a ball) with one's head.
A footgoer; pedestrian
A line of information printed at the bottom of a page to identify the contents or number pages. (Compare foot in printing.)
Something that measures a stated number of feet in some dimension.

examples.text: The new boat is a six-footer.

glosses: Someone who has a preference for using a certain foot.

examples.text: a right-footer

glosses: Football / soccer.
A football.

examples.text: […] punting a footer around the quad on a beautiful day like today, not frowsting in their studies.

glosses: To meddle with or pass time without accomplishing anything meaningful.
The title or short title of a volume printed at the top of left-hand text pages or sometimes of all text pages.
Alternative form of running headline.

examples.text: Another unexpected issue was faced when the word fuckʼs position as the first entry on the left-hand page of a double-page spread meant it was automatically used for the page's running head[.]

glosses: A word under the right-hand side of the last line on a book page that repeats the first word on the following page.
The last word of a speech, serving as a cue for the next speaker.
A word or expression repeated until it becomes representative of a party, school, business, or point of view.

examples.text: One could give a long list of such intellectual fashions and catchwords which in the course of two or three generations have in turn dominated the thinking of the intellectual.

The war itself has several names, including "the famine war" (ḥarb al-majā'a) and seferberlik, a Turkish word, meaning "travel by land," that began its wartime career as a reference to "military conscription" but quickly became a catchword for all the calamities and suffering experienced by civilians.

glosses: Frase o palabra con que se enuncia el asunto o nombre de una obra, o alguna de sus partes o capítulos.

examples.text: ¿Por qué creen que Gabriel García Márquez puso como título «Cien años de soledad» a su novela?

glosses: Nombre de una obra artística en general.

examples.text: Sí, el título es «Damián»; y lo consigues en cualquier librería.

glosses: Distintivo con el que se le conoce a alguien, ya sea por sus cualidades o acciones.

examples.text: Cleopatra tenía el título de «la boca de los diez mil hombres.

glosses: Dícese de alguna dignidad nobiliaria o de la persona que la posee.
Honor o distinción que alguien logra conseguir, especialmente en algún concurso o campeonato.
Razón, causa, motivo o pretexto.

examples.text: No tener título para excusarse.

glosses: Dícese de cada una de las partes principales en las que se dividen y subdividen las leyes y reglamentos.
Instrumento o testimonio dado para desempeñar un empleo o profesión.
Instrumento legal que explica o legitima la posesión o transmisión de un derecho real.
Acto por el que se transmite un derecho real.
Documento que refrenda tal acto.
En particular, documento que refrenda un crédito contra otra persona o entidad, o la posesión de acciones.
Honor o distinción concedida al vencedor en un campeonato o competencia deportiva.

examples.text: Gané ese título después de vencer al equipo contrario en un campeonato de vóleibol.

glosses: Cuantificación de la proporción de una solución.
